definitions.explanation: A hereditary emblem used to identify a Japanese family, clan, or household. Originating in the Heian period, family crests feature stylized designs based on plants, animals, geometric shapes, or other motifs. They appear on formal clothing, tombstones, and traditional items.

examples.japanese: うちの{家紋|かもん}は{桐|きり}だ。
examples.english: Our family crest is the paulownia.

examples.japanese: {着物|きもの}に{家紋|かもん}が{入|はい}っている。
examples.english: The kimono has a family crest on it.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}の{家紋|かもん}を{知|し}らない{人|ひと}が{最近|さいきん}は{増|ふ}えているらしい。
examples.english: Apparently, more and more people these days don't know their own family crest.

notes:
USAGE: {家紋|かもん} are found on formal kimono ({紋付|もんつき}), gravestones, {提灯|ちょうちん} (paper lanterns), and family-owned items. Common motifs include {桐|きり} (paulownia), {菊|きく} (chrysanthemum), and {梅|うめ} (plum blossom).

Historically, samurai families used {家紋|かもん} to identify themselves on the battlefield. Today, they are most commonly seen at weddings, funerals, and other formal ceremonies.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {家紋|かもん}が{入|はい}る: to bear a family crest
- {家紋|かもん}{入|い}りの{着物|きもの}: kimono with a family crest
- {家紋|かもん}を{調|しら}べる: to look up one's family crest
